guidance: Marking arithmetic only. Measure every line to its outside edge, square the court from the net line with the tapes, and check local planning rules and the space for umpires, benches and fencing before fixing the run-back.
method: The ITF Rules of Tennis make the court a 23.77 m rectangle, 10.97 m wide for doubles and 8.23 m for singles, with the net across the middle, and every measurement is taken to the outside of the lines. The service lines sit 6.40 m from the net and are drawn only between the singles sidelines, so each is 8.23 m long on either kind of court and the 1.37 m doubles alleys never widen a service box; the centre service line runs 12.80 m from one service line to the other and splits each service area into boxes 6.40 m deep and 4.115 m wide (4.11 m in the rule book's table), and each baseline carries a 10 cm centre mark. The tool sums the painted length of two baselines, two doubles sidelines and two singles sidelines on a combined court (two baselines and two singles sidelines on a singles-only court), two 8.23 m service lines, the 12.80 m centre service line and two 10 cm centre marks: 146.48 m for a combined court and 93.46 m for a singles-only one. Paint area is that length times the line width, and paint per coat is the area divided by the coverage entered; the small overlaps where lines cross are not deducted. Appendix X supplies the marking-out figures the page lists: a 12.80 m net line between post centres, the inner sideline at 4.11 m, the singles sticks at 5.03 m, the outer sidelines at 5.48 m and the net posts at 6.40 m from the centre, then the 16.18 m diagonal and 11.89 m sideline tapes that meet at a baseline corner, with a 10.97 m baseline check; a singles-only court uses a 10 m net, 5.03 m to each post, a 14.46 m diagonal and an 8.23 m baseline check. The full-court diagonal is the square root of the length squared plus the width squared, 26.18 m for doubles and 25.15 m for singles. The footprint is the court plus the ITF's recommended minimum run-back, 5.48 m behind the baselines and 3.05 m beside the sidelines for club and recreational play or 6.40 m and 3.66 m for international competition; it is a planning rectangle, not a boundary, and local rules may ask for more. Net figures follow Rule 1: posts 1.07 m high, 0.914 m outside the court, and a net 0.914 m high at the centre, held by singles sticks 0.914 m outside each singles sideline when a doubles net is used for singles. Line width is accepted from 2.5 to 5 cm, the range Rule 1 sets for court lines apart from the 10 cm baseline allowance, and paint coverage from 1 to 50 square metres per litre. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: ITF Rules of Tennis 2026 - Rule 1 (court 23.77 m long, 10.97 m wide for doubles and 8.23 m for singles, service lines 6.40 m from the net, net posts 0.914 m outside the court) and Appendix X (marking out a court: 12.80 m net line, the 4.11, 5.03, 5.48 and 6.40 m points, the 16.18 m and 11.89 m tapes, and the 5.48/3.05 m club and 6.40/3.66 m international run-back minimums)
